title: Hypertrophy Q&A #6
summary: NH answers training questions: mixing volume and intensity in each session, squat variations for quads, rest periods, machines that hurt, fixing arm imbalances, teenagers and sport, dead hangs vs barbell holds, oblique training and waist size, fat-pad benches, V-taper exercises, leg length differences, failure versus fixed reps in evolving schemes, regional hypertrophy, the SSB, genetics, band training, calisthenics limits and why you must program.
claims: NH dislikes separate volume and intensity days: volume days become junk volume and sandbagging, intensity days push poor form and too little volume
Mixing low and high reps in the same session is complementary, e.g. an intense strength set followed by 3x3 back-off sets
For bodybuilding every day should be a volume day, just with variation in volume
Front squats are great but too hard to master; there's no in-between, and unmastered they're useless for hypertrophy
Paused squats are NH's favorite quad variation: safe when done upright, no stretch reflex, great quad tension and carryover to the squat
Paused squats only tax the lower back if you good-morning the weight
Second favorite: parallel box squat with a close stance, carrying over to both squat and deadlift
The good morning may be the best non-squat lift for carryover, but it gives no quad volume
Rest as little as possible while staying performant: typically 1.5-3 minutes, up to 5; more than 5 is overkill
If you can repeat a 1RM after 10 minutes rest, it wasn't a true max
Shorter rests of 60-90 s improve conditioning but hinder performance, turning lifts into cardio
Feeling a ligament burn instead of the muscle signals a problem; some machines just fit badly, so switch exercises
Free weights let you arrange body and bar around each other; machines force one path
Padded standing calf raise machines are usually too vertical and are bad for spine, knees and calf growth
To fix an arm imbalance, give the smaller side more volume while maintaining the stronger side with a few high-intensity sets; don't shrink the strong side
Maintaining muscle takes much less work than building it
NH's bigger arm is not his stronger arm; poorer leverage forces the weaker side to be bigger to lift the same weight
A 14-year-old lifting four days a week plus boxing is doing too much; do 2-3 full-body sessions instead
Teens 14-17 should prioritize proper form, work capacity and a good relationship with training over muscle gains
Dead hangs carry over better to vertical pulls, barbell holds to horizontal pulls: specificity
Barbell holds build more grip strength; dead hangs give a more aggressive forearm stretch since all load goes through the arms
The waist is mostly bone structure; training the core only thickens the abdominal wall and obliques somewhat
Bulking can widen the waist via visceral fat
People with naturally wide waists, like NH, might as well sculpt their core
Resting obliques can look like love handles from some angles, but flexed they taper the waist
Explosive movements can still cause hypertrophy; slow negatives aren't required for growth
Oblique isolation exercises rarely work the obliques; heavy squats and deadlifts grow them
A thick wide 'fat pad' bench lets your back dig in so you don't slide, and keeps both shoulder blades on the bench for shoulder health
Both shoulder blades need to be on the bench; narrow commercial benches cause shoulder issues
A fat pad limits depth and elbow tuck, so try before buying
V-taper is shoulder-to-waist ratio illusion: pullovers for ribcage expansion, pull-ups for outer lats, lateral raises and face pulls for side and rear delts
Front delts add thickness but not width, so they don't help the V-taper
Seated lateral raises reduce cheating for people who feel traps instead of delts
Triceps long head adds width and back-pose thickness, helping the V-taper
Deadlifting the day after 3-4 sets of pull-ups is fine; you can even superset them
Pull-ups barely carry over to the deadlift since they don't involve the posterior chain
Almost everyone has a slight leg length difference; don't put something under your foot; it only matters when substantial
Moving one foot slightly out in your stance compensates for a hip shift
Big hip shifts are mainly dangerous when jumping to unfamiliar heavy weights
NH trains everything to failure except strength work, where he leaves 1 RIR
Failure means stopping one rep short of failing a rep; never fail a rep, as it shows you don't know your limits and derails the workout
Two types of evolving rep schemes: open ranges like 8-12 where you take every rep, and fixed rep targets like 5-4 or 6-5-4 for strength work where you stop at the target even with reps left
Stopping at the strength target keeps strength a step or two ahead and prevents plateaus; make up extra volume in later sets
Proper sandbagging is sandbagging just enough never to stop progressing; poor sandbagging fails to challenge the muscle
Form tweaks shift tension to parts of a muscle, but every movement works the whole muscle
Squats grow the quad sweep but can neglect the VMO; front squat to a box trains the VMO well, or use leg extensions
Dumbbell bench is an acceptable replacement for barbell bench; tuck the elbows
The SSB pushes you forward into a hinge, while a front squat pulls you to round; front squatting with an SSB is valid, but SSB back squats are nothing like front squats
Looking big at low bodyweight indicates good insertions and small joints, good genetics for bodybuilding as an illusion game
Fast recovery and low soreness come mostly from built work capacity rather than genetics
With only 30 kg, combine weights and bands for lower reps to failure rather than 50 easy pump reps; supersets can raise relative intensity
Calisthenics alone can't max upper-body development: they lack loading for upper traps, rhomboids and erectors and lack triceps long head, wrist flexion and neck work
Calisthenics develop the front well: chest, shoulders (with handstand push-ups), triceps and abs
Long-armed lifters must simply train and get very big for arms to look proportional
With a sport, the novice template is fine; start at 2 days or pause the sport for two weeks; if the sport is the priority, make lifting sport-specific and secondary
Picking workouts by what looks small that day lets body dysmorphia dictate training; instinctive training doesn't work except for beginners or steroid users
Everything you do in the gym is a program, even a bad one; start small and program
